data.narrative:
Aeva Technologies is a public-stage semiconductor company founded by Soroush Salehian and Mina Rezk, currently valued at $1.09B with $660M+ raised to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 public-stage semiconductor comparables: Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), and Ouster ($2.3B).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given data availability. Aeva's 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables yield a median valuation of $35.8B, with a range spanning $2.3B to $39.2B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in the semiconductor subsector—capital intensity, commercialization progress, and market focus drive substantial valuation variance even among public peers. The peer-median method cannot be cross-checked against price-to-sales anchoring because Aeva's revenue is not on file; public semiconductor multiples (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) show a sector median P/S of 21.4x, but application requires disclosed revenue.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $30.4B to $41.2B, with a median estimate of $35.8B. This band is grounded in one method only, creating material uncertainty. The wide peer dispersion ($2.3B–$39.2B) underscores that stage and sector alone are weak predictors; revenue traction, addressable market capture, and path to profitability remain unmeasured against available data. Resolution of valuation dispersion depends on revenue disclosure and margin trajectory.
